x-bump-note: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 (top-level-array-additive, claude-klabauter-first) adds optional top-level `shapes` [shapeEntry] (DR-201 (b)); holding, because fleet.aggregate_capability_index validates manifests with additionalProperties false, so no declared-tolerant consumer set exists. Pending DoE's own copy (DoE I47 C2). RE-VENDOR: coordinator-content-repo.
description: The AGGREGATED fleet-capability index — the shape the engine repo's engine op produces by reading every platform repo's authored capability-manifest.schema.json instance and folding them into one persisted, read-derived projection (docs/plans/2026-07-17-cross-repo-capability-lens.md § C1). This is a Tier-B aggregation VIEW, not a producer sink: no repo ever emits INTO this index (Fleet Producer Contract, docs/wiki/hook-best-practices/state-placement-law.md § Fleet Producer Contract, lines ~290-293 — a consolidation point a repo writes into would make one producer a fleet-wide SPOF). If lost or stale it is fully rebuildable from the decentralized per-repo manifests, which remain the sole source of truth. The review SKILL (C4) resolves this index via the engine op-invocation seam, applies the read-time TTL staleness downgrade (AC8) against `generated_at`/`ttl`, and passes its path to prior-art-checker (C3) as `fleet_capability_index:`. `entries[].host_repo` mirrors capability-manifest.schema.json's per-capability shape (duplicated here, not $ref'd cross-file, because this repo's schema-validation harness only resolves `$ref`/`$defs` within a single schema file — see coordinator/bin/lib/schema.js's JSON-Schema-subset validator) and MUST include every repo's capabilities, INCLUDING the plan's own repo, so the checker can compute `host_repo == plan_repo` asymmetry (F1c) as a mechanical field comparison rather than an external lookup.

generated_at.description: ISO timestamp this aggregated index was last (re)built by the engine's op. Paired with `ttl` for the read-time TTL staleness rule (AC8): past `generated_at` + `ttl`, the review SKILL downgrades every entry's `maturity` to stale/unverified before passing the index on, so a silently-stale-but-readable index is never trusted as live.

ttl.description: Freshness stamp — the declared time-to-live for this index build (e.g. an ISO-8601 duration like "P1D"), read alongside `generated_at` by the review SKILL's read-time TTL downgrade rule (AC8/F2). Distinct from any single manifest's `refresh_cadence` (capability-manifest.schema.json): this is the INDEX's own staleness budget, set by the engine's refresh ceremony, not a per-repo authoring cadence.

entries.description: Every aggregated capability entry across every enumerated sibling repo, INCLUDING the plan's own repo's entries if it has authored a manifest (F1c — required so `host_repo == plan_repo` is a mechanical comparison the checker can run without a separate self-lookup). May be empty for an OSS-safe degrade (registry absent, zero siblings enumerated, or zero manifests found) — an empty `entries[]` is a valid index, not a validation failure.

shapes.description: OPTIONAL. Copy-out exemplar shapes aggregated across every enumerated sibling repo (DR-201 shapeEntry, carried through from each source manifest with `source_repo` and verbatim `maturity`).

shape_id.description: Stable identifier for this shape, unique within the emitting repo's manifest.

shape_label.description: Human-readable label; the string a copy-out offer quotes verbatim.

shape_summary.description: One-line summary of what the shape is and when to copy it.

exemplar_path.description: Repo-relative path of the exemplar in the owning repo.

copy_posture.description: Whether a consumer may copy the exemplar out directly or must ask the owning repo first.

maturity.description: Fail-closed reachability marker, carried through verbatim from the source manifest.

provenance.description: Same enum and semantics as indexEntry.provenance.

source_repo.description: The emitting repo: a non-polarity echo of the manifest-level `host_repo`, never compared for consume suppression.

indexEntry.description: Same per-capability shape as capability-manifest.schema.json's `capabilityEntry`, PLUS the emitting repo's `host_repo` present on every entry (required at this level too, not only inherited from a manifest-level field, since entries from many manifests are flattened into one array here).

capability_id.description: Stable identifier for this capability, unique within its emitting repo's manifest — see capability-manifest.schema.json.

capability_class.description: Coarse structural class — the field the prior-art-checker's construction-vs-production predicate (F1a) matches a plan's proposed-artifact-class against.

capability_label.description: Human-readable label, e.g. "workstate store" — paired with `capability_class` for the domain-aware match (F1b).

consume_seam.description: REAL, structured consume seam vouched for by the emitting repo — carried through aggregation unchanged from the source manifest.

maturity.description: Fail-closed reachability marker (AC9), as authored in the source manifest. The review SKILL (C4) may further DOWNGRADE (never upgrade) this value at read-time per the TTL staleness rule (AC8) once the index itself has aged past its `ttl` — that downgrade happens outside this schema, at consumption time, and is not itself validated here.

provenance.description: Three-value provenance marker carried through from the source manifest (capability-manifest.schema.json); `generated`/`asserted` fail closed harder than `curated` on maturity (AC9).

host_repo.description: The offering repo for this entry. CRITICAL (F1c): every entry — INCLUDING entries whose `host_repo` equals the plan's own repo — MUST be present so the checker's `host_repo == plan_repo` suppression is a mechanical field comparison over this array, never an external per-repo lookup.
